chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jahm ibn Abi Juheyma, from one of the freedmen of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him said:

A man from Quraish was with Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and he began mentioning Quraish and the Arabs. Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him at that: 'Leave this! The people are three: an Arab, a Mawla (freedman/client), and an 'Ilj (foreigner/outsider). So we are the Arabs, and our Shias are the Mawali, and whoever is not upon what we are upon, he is an 'Ilj.' The Quraishi said: 'You are saying this, O Abu Al-Hasan, so where are the prided ones (afkhadh) of Quraish and the Arabs?' Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'It is as I have said to you.'

key_terms.أَفْخَاذ: Afkhdh, plural of fakhidh, meaning prided ones or prominent clans
key_terms.الْعَرَب: Arabs, referring to the broader Arab identity
key_terms.شِيعَتُنَا: Our Shia, the followers of the Imams
key_terms.عِلْج: Ilj, a foreigner or outsider, here referring to those outside the Shia fold
key_terms.قُرَيْش: Quraish, the prominent tribe of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.مَوْلًى: Mawla, a freedman or client, here referring to the Shia followers

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Musa al-Kazim define the true 'Arabs' in contrast to tribal lineage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) redefines Arab identity through a Shia theological lens, prioritizing spiritual lineage and adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt over tribal genealogy. He categorizes humanity into three tiers: the Imams as the true 'Arabs' (leaders), their Shia followers as 'Mawali' (freedmen/clients), and those outside this spiritual fold as 'Ilj' (foreigners/outsiders). This classification underscores the Shia concept of 'Wilayah' as the primary marker of distinction, effectively elevating the status of the broader community through connection to the Imams while demoting mere tribal prestige.
